properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **BOTH (a) AND (b).** A served interview step carries *when and what to ask* — in domain language only — and a served routing table carries *how the user's words map to node types*, plus which artifacts to expect for that kind of thing. His reasoning: **neither half is useful alone.** A skill without a table leaves the mapping improvised, which is the failure Alex hit; a table without a skill is never consulted. Option (c), leaving it to agent judgement, is closed — it has now been observed failing on the second user's first real project. Option (d), detecting it, stays rejected-for-a-reason: the evidence never enters the graph.

⇒ SATISFIES `req:the-kind-of-system-is-established-before-its-parts-are-captured` (captured the same day on Anthony's word, from Alex's report). This decision settles HOW that requirement is delivered; the requirement states WHAT is owed.

⭐⭐ THE PRIOR ART SETTLES THE SHAPE, AND ONLY HALF OF IT SURVIVES — `reflow/workflows/00b-framework_selection.json`, read 2026-08-14 at Anthony's pointer:
  · **THE TERMINOLOGY REGISTRY** (`definitions/framework_registry.json`: node → `service`/`gene`/`agent`/`species`) was CORRECTLY REJECTED by `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` (now `dropped`) — cosmetic renaming, plus a load-bearing claim that *"framework choice determines which NetworkX analyses are available"*, which gates capability on a self-declared label. **The routing table decided here is NOT that**: it maps the user's phrasing to reflow2's own unchanged vocabulary, and gates nothing.
  · **THE SEMANTIC-MATCHING INTERVIEW** is what survives, and it is not cosmetic. S-01A: *"Framework selection is an ARCHITECTURAL DECISION, not a configuration choice. Wrong framework = wrong insights."* LESSON-04: *"Framework abstractions must match system semantics. Workflows are state machines (not services), even though both could be 'engineered systems'."* **Its first action is "Ask user to describe the system" — domain language, not node types.**

🛑 **AND THE DROPPED REQUIREMENT HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN THE SURVIVOR.** `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` closes: *"domain as a hint to EXTRACTION and phrasing — what vocabulary the agent uses when talking to the user and reading their documents — without ever gating which computations run. That keeps the honest part of reflow's insight (a biologist should not be told about 'services')."* It was dropped as a registry, its surviving half was named in its own text, **nobody built it, and the second user then walked into exactly that gap.** A road correctly not taken left a fork nobody came back for.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14.

HIS WORDS: *"It was a little unsure of how to store the data models for my project in the graph. It asked me what node types it should store them as. I didn't really know for sure so I told it to figure it out. It worked, but that might be confusing for someone who isn't technical… it should probably ask probing questions to figure this out without exposing internal components of the graph structure to the user."*

⭐ THE INVERSION IS THE FINDING. Mapping a person's words onto node types IS the agent's job and is written down as such — `capture-intent` exists to turn what the user said into Requirements / Capabilities / Components / Interfaces, and `describe_schema` exists so the AGENT can discover the vocabulary rather than guess. **The agent had both and handed the question back to the user anyway.** The schema is not under-documented here; the labour was returned to the one person in the room with no reason to know the answer.

🛑 AND REFLOW2 CANNOT SEE THIS HAPPEN. Every detector reasons over nodes already in the graph, and a leaked question leaves no node — the user's confusion lives in the conversation, never in the record. `loop_status` would have read perfectly clean through the whole exchange. **Same shape as `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`: a discipline that exists only as an instruction, with nothing able to observe whether it held.** That is the standing argument for why the table matters as much as the skill line: a table can be wrong in public, an improvisation cannot.

📌 IT ALSO WORKED, WHICH IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART. He said *"I told it to figure it out"* and the result was fine. So the cost is not a wrong graph — it is that a non-technical user meeting the same prompt has no such escape, and answering it wrongly would put their design in the wrong shape without either party noticing.

THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD.
(a) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — an interview step in the skills: never ask for a node type; ask about the thing itself and do the mapping yourself.
(b) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — a served routing table, phrasing → node type, plus expected artifacts per kind of thing. Precedent: `capture-session` ships one and its first dogfood found a hole in it.
(c) LEAVE IT TO AGENT JUDGEMENT — **CLOSED**, observed failing.
(d) DETECT IT — rejected for a reason: the evidence never enters the graph, so any check would have to live in the harness and read the conversation.

⚠️ ONE HONEST TENSION, UNCHANGED BY THE DECISION: some vocabulary reaching the user is CORRECT. `where-am-i` reports the design back in their words and gap questions are deliberately plain, so the rule is *never make the user choose the internal category* — not *never say a word from the schema*. Drawn loosely it would produce a skill that fights `describe_schema`'s legitimate use.
properties.name: DECIDED — the agent never asks the user to pick a node type: a served interview step carries WHEN and WHAT to ask, a served routing table carries HOW their words map
properties.rationale: Raised under the brainstorm skill from Alex's report and settled the same day on Anthony's word, after reading the reflow prior art he pointed at. The reading changed the shape of the answer: reflow's S-01A turns out to contain two separable things, and reflow2 had dropped both together when only the terminology registry deserved it. Recording that split matters because the surviving half — the semantic-matching interview — was already named in the dropped requirement's own closing paragraph, and a future session finding `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` at `dropped` would otherwise reasonably conclude the whole idea was rejected.
